item.title: The Lambda Calculus and Its Racket Implementation
item.description: The lambda calculus (also written as λ-calculus) is a formal system for expressing computation based on function abstraction and application using variable binding and substitution. The calculus is a universal machine: a model of computation that can be used to simulate any Turing machine. Alonzo Church introduced it in the 1930s as part of his research into the foundations of mathematics. Racket implements it directly: lambda is the abstraction, and (f a) is the application.
